claim: Fiber photometry recordings from CeA Vgat neurons in awake, behaving mice were performed to assess the activity of CeA neurons in relation to evoked itch/scratch behaviors.
source: We performed fiber photometry recordings from CeA Vgat neurons in awake, behaving mice to assess the activity of CeA neurons in relation to evoked itch/scratch behaviors.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental method used to record CeA neuronal activity during itch behaviors.

claim: GCaMP6s was expressed in CeA GABAergic neurons using viral delivery of Cre-dependent GCaMP6s in Vgat-IRES-Cre mice.
source: To record real-time Ca2+ dynamics in the CeA (Cui et al., 2013), we expressed the genetically encoded calcium indicator, GCaMP6s, in CeA GABAergic neurons using viral delivery of Cre-dependent GCaMP6s in Vgat-IRES-Cre mice (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–c).
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental approach and cites a prior method (Cui et al., 2013).

claim: The majority of CeA neurons are GABAergic.
source: As the majority of CeA neurons are GABAergic (Swanson and Petrovich, 1998), this approach allows us to target the CeA and avoid picking up photometry signals from neighboring BLA neurons, as could occur if we used non Cre-dependent GCaMP6.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Swanson and Petrovich, 1998).

claim: Subcutaneous injection of chloroquine in the nape of the neck induced scratching behavior and resulted in robust increases in CeA neuronal activity.
source: Subcutaneous injection of chloroquine in the nape of the neck induced scratching behavior and resulted in robust increases in CeA neuronal activity (Figure 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: CeA neuronal activity commenced with initiation of scratching and stabilized whenever scratching stopped.
source: This activity commenced with initiation of scratching and stabilized whenever scratching stopped (Figure 1c–e), suggesting that the elevated activity was tightly coupled with the act of scratching.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1c-e.

claim: The elevated CeA neuronal activity was tightly coupled with the act of scratching.
source: This activity commenced with initiation of scratching and stabilized whenever scratching stopped (Figure 1c–e), suggesting that the elevated activity was tightly coupled with the act of scratching.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal relationship between neuronal activity and scratching behavior.

claim: Activity-dependent mapping studies show robust cFos labeling bilaterally in the CeA following chloroquine injection in the nape of the neck compared to saline-injected mice.
source: Consistent with these real-time dynamic recordings, activity-dependent mapping studies show robust cFos labeling bilaterally in the CeA following chloroquine injection in the nape of the neck compared to saline-injected mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–c.

claim: No significant differences in cFos labeling were observed between right and left CeA.
source: We observed no significant differences in cFos labeling between right and left CeA (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: The CeA is thought to play a critical role in learning and modifying sensory and emotional memories and translating this information into apt adaptive behaviors.
source: The central amygdala (CeA) represents a strong candidate for these functions as the CeA is thought to play a critical role in learning and modifying sensory and emotional memories and translating this information into apt adaptive behaviors (Fadok et al., 2018; Gründemann and Lüthi, 2015; LeDoux and Daw, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Recent studies have implicated the CeA in the regulation of itch.
source: Recent studies have implicated the CeA in the regulation of itch (Albisetti et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2016; Ehling et al., 2018; Mu et al., 2017), and elevated activity in the CeA has been seen in patients during experimental itch (Papoiu et al., 2014; Vierow et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Elevated activity in the CeA has been seen in patients during experimental itch.
source: Recent studies have implicated the CeA in the regulation of itch (Albisetti et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2016; Ehling et al., 2018; Mu et al., 2017), and elevated activity in the CeA has been seen in patients during experimental itch (Papoiu et al., 2014; Vierow et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: FosTRAPing with chloroquine treatment produced robust tdTomato expression in both the right and left CeA.
source: FosTRAPing with chloroquine treatment produced robust tdTomato expression in both the right and left CeA (Figure 2c–e), and small number of neurons in saline-treated controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e–g), consistent with our cFos staining results above.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2c-e.

claim: FosTRAPing with saline treatment produced a small number of tdTomato-expressing neurons.
source: FosTRAPing with chloroquine treatment produced robust tdTomato expression in both the right and left CeA (Figure 2c–e), and small number of neurons in saline-treated controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e–g), consistent with our cFos staining results above.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1e–g.

claim: The small population of saline TRAPed neurons could be due to the needle stick during the injection itself, and thus could label some pain-responsive CeA neurons.
source: This small population of saline TRAPed neurons could be due to the needle stick during the injection itself, and thus could label some pain-responsive CeA neurons.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: The majority of the tdTomato-positive CeA FosTRAPed neurons faithfully overlap with cFos-positive cells.
source: The majority of the tdTomato-positive CeA FosTRAPed neurons faithfully overlap with cFos-positive cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data described in the text and shown in Figure 2c, f.

claim: Optogenetic reactivation of FosTRAPed (ChR2+) right CeA neurons resulted in significant spontaneous scratching and grooming behaviors compared to pre-stimulation baseline and photostimulation of eYFP-expressing control mice.
source: Optogenetic reactivation of FosTRAPed (ChR2+) right CeA neurons resulted in significant spontaneous scratching and grooming behaviors compared to pre-stimulation baseline and photostimulation of eYFP-expressing control mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data described in the text and shown in Figure 2h.

claim: Spontaneous scratching and grooming behaviors were directed all over the body, not restricted to the nape of the neck where the pruritogen injection was administered for the TRAP.
source: Interestingly, although ChR2 was FosTRAPed by injecting chloroquine into the nape of the neck, we observed spontaneous scratching and grooming behaviors directed all over the body (data not shown) in a stimulation frequency-dependent manner (Figure 2h, i).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and data shown in Figures 2h, i.

claim: Spontaneous scratching and grooming behaviors occurred in a stimulation frequency-dependent manner.
source: Interestingly, although ChR2 was FosTRAPed by injecting chloroquine into the nape of the neck, we observed spontaneous scratching and grooming behaviors directed all over the body (data not shown) in a stimulation frequency-dependent manner (Figure 2h, i).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2i.

claim: Elicitation of scratching behaviors is not lateralized to the right CeA.
source: Even though some functions of the CeA are lateralized (Carrasquillo and Gereau, 2007), elicitation of scratching behaviors is not lateralized to the right CeA as optical stimulation of FosTRAPed ChR2+ neurons in the left CeA also resulted in significant spontaneous scratching behaviors compared to pre-stimulation baseline and photostimulation of eYFP-expressing controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and a citation to prior work (Carrasquillo and Gereau, 2007).

claim: Optical stimulation of FosTRAPed ChR2+ neurons in the left CeA resulted in significant spontaneous scratching behaviors compared to pre-stimulation baseline and photostimulation of eYFP-expressing controls.
source: Even though some functions of the CeA are lateralized (Carrasquillo and Gereau, 2007), elicitation of scratching behaviors is not lateralized to the right CeA as optical stimulation of FosTRAPed ChR2+ neurons in the left CeA also resulted in significant spontaneous scratching behaviors compared to pre-stimulation baseline and photostimulation of eYFP-expressing controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Chemogenetic activation of FosTRAPed CeA neurons resulted in significant spontaneous scratching behaviors.
source: Chemogenetic activation of FosTRAPed CeA neurons also resulted in significant spontaneous scratching behaviors (Figure 2—figure supplement 3e), consistent with the optogenetic results.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3e.

claim: Stimulation of FosTRAPed neurons has no significant effect on hindpaw thermal sensitivity.
source: In contrast, stimulation of FosTRAPed neurons has no significant effect on hindpaw thermal sensitivity (Figure 2—figure supplement 4b) or licking and biting behaviors.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4b.

claim: Stimulation of FosTRAPed neurons has no significant effect on licking and biting behaviors.
source: In contrast, stimulation of FosTRAPed neurons has no significant effect on hindpaw thermal sensitivity (Figure 2—figure supplement 4b) or licking and biting behaviors.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations described in the text.

claim: Stimulation of FosTRAPed neurons slightly increased mechanical sensitivity.
source: However, stimulation of FosTRAPed neurons slightly increased mechanical sensitivity, suggesting that these neurons can encode generalized scratching behavior and hypersensitivity to mechanical stimuli (Figure 2—figure supplement 4c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4c.

claim: FosTRAPed neurons can encode generalized scratching behavior and hypersensitivity to mechanical stimuli.
source: However, stimulation of FosTRAPed neurons slightly increased mechanical sensitivity, suggesting that these neurons can encode generalized scratching behavior and hypersensitivity to mechanical stimuli (Figure 2—figure supplement 4c).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observation of increased mechanical sensitivity.

claim: FosTRAPed neurons might be involved in nociceptive processing.
source: These results suggest that FosTRAPed neurons might be involved in nociceptive processing (Neugebauer and Li, 2002).
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation supported by a citation to prior work (Neugebauer and Li, 2002).

claim: Chloroquine-evoked scratching was potentiated with optical reactivation of CeA chloroquine-TRAPed neurons while no changes were observed in the eYFP controls.
source: Chloroquine-evoked scratching was potentiated with optical reactivation of CeA chloroquine-TRAPed neurons while no changes were observed in the eYFP controls (Figure 2j).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2j.

claim: Chemogenetic stimulation of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons potentiated chloroquine-evoked scratching.
source: Chemogenetic stimulation of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons produced similar results (Figure 2—figure supplement 3h).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3h.

claim: Itch is an aversive sensory experience in humans and rodents.
source: Itch is an aversive sensory experience in humans and rodents (Desbordes et al., 2015; Mochizuki et al., 2015; Mochizuki et al., 2014; Papoiu et al., 2012; Papoiu et al., 2013), and the CeA mediates aversive phenotypes (Carrasquillo and Gereau, 2007; Ciocchi et al., 2010; Ehrlich et al., 2009; Haubensak et al., 2010; Tovote et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The CeA mediates aversive phenotypes.
source: Itch is an aversive sensory experience in humans and rodents (Desbordes et al., 2015; Mochizuki et al., 2015; Mochizuki et al., 2014; Papoiu et al., 2012; Papoiu et al., 2013), and the CeA mediates aversive phenotypes (Carrasquillo and Gereau, 2007; Ciocchi et al., 2010; Ehrlich et al., 2009; Haubensak et al., 2010; Tovote et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Reactivation of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons produced robust place aversion to the stimulated side of the chamber while eYFP-FosTRAPed controls did not.
source: Reactivation of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons produced robust place aversion to the stimulated side of the chamber while eYFP-FosTRAPed controls did not (Figure 3b–d), thus demonstrating that chloroquine-activated CeA neurons carry negative reinforcement signals.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3b-d.

claim: Chloroquine-activated CeA neurons carry negative reinforcement signals.
source: Reactivation of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons produced robust place aversion to the stimulated side of the chamber while eYFP-FosTRAPed controls did not (Figure 3b–d), thus demonstrating that chloroquine-activated CeA neurons carry negative reinforcement signals.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observation of place aversion.

claim: Patients with pruritic skin disorders exhibit heightened anxiety.
source: Patients with pruritic skin disorders exhibit heightened anxiety (Ginsburg, 1995), and prior studies have shown CeA as a critical hub in coordinating anxiety states (Ahrens et al., 2018; Shackman and Fox, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Ginsburg, 1995).

claim: Prior studies have shown CeA as a critical hub in coordinating anxiety states.
source: Patients with pruritic skin disorders exhibit heightened anxiety (Ginsburg, 1995), and prior studies have shown CeA as a critical hub in coordinating anxiety states (Ahrens et al., 2018; Shackman and Fox, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Optogenetic and chemogenetic reactivation of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons leads to a profound decrease in time spent in the open arms of EZM compared to controls, indicating anxiogenic-like behavioral state.
source: Optogenetic and chemogenetic reactivation of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons leads to a profound decrease in time spent in the open arms of EZM compared to controls, indicating anxiogenic-like behavioral state (Figure 3e, Figure 3—figure supplement 1b, c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3e and Figure 3—figure supplement 1b, c.

claim: Reactivation of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons leads to decreased time spent in the center during the OFT, suggesting that these neurons can drive anxiety-like behavior.
source: Reactivation of these neurons also leads to decreased time spent in the center during the OFT, further suggesting that these neurons can drive anxiety-like behavior (Figure 3—figure supplement 1d–i).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1d–i.

claim: Opto- and chemogenetic reactivation of FosTRAPed neurons did not drive freezing or flight responses in OFT.
source: Notably, opto- and chemogenetic reactivation of FosTRAPed neurons did not drive freezing or flight responses in OFT (Figure 3—figure supplement 1e, g), suggesting that these neurons are not involved in fear-like behaviors.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1e, g.

claim: Chloroquine-TRAPed neurons are not involved in fear-like behaviors.
source: Notably, opto- and chemogenetic reactivation of FosTRAPed neurons did not drive freezing or flight responses in OFT (Figure 3—figure supplement 1e, g), suggesting that these neurons are not involved in fear-like behaviors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observation that reactivation did not drive freezing or flight responses.

claim: Stimulation of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons had no effect on feeding and other appetitive behaviors the CeA is reported to evoke.
source: Furthermore, stimulation of these neurons also had no effect on feeding and other appetitive behaviors the CeA is reported to evoke (Douglass et al., 2017; Han et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2017; Li et al., 2017; Figure 3—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplements 2 and 3 and citations to prior work.

claim: Chemogenetic inhibition of CeA chloroquine-TRAPed neurons by CNO injection significantly attenuated chloroquine-evoked scratching compared to pre-CNO baseline and compared to mCherry-expressing controls.
source: Chemogenetic inhibition of CeA chloroquine-TRAPed neurons by CNO injection significantly attenuated chloroquine-evoked scratching compared to pre-CNO baseline and compared to mCherry-expressing controls (Figure 4e, f).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4e, f.

claim: Chloroquine-activated (chloroquine-TRAPed) CeA neurons are necessary for chloroquine-induced scratching behavior.
source: These results suggest that chloroquine-activated (chloroquine-TRAPed) CeA neurons are necessary for chloroquine-induced scratching behavior.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observation that inhibition of these neurons attenuated scratching.

claim: Inhibiting CeA chloroquine-TRAPed neurons had no significant effect on thermal or mechanical sensitivity.
source: We observed no significant effect on thermal or mechanical sensitivity by inhibiting CeA chloroquine-TRAPed neurons (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Silencing CeA chloroquine-TRAPed neurons did not lead to freezing or flight responses or anxiolytic effects.
source: Furthermore, silencing CeA chloroquine-TRAPed neurons did not lead to freezing or flight responses or anxiolytic effects (Figure 3—figure supplement 1j–n).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1j–n.

claim: Inhibition of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons did not affect feeding and appetitive behaviors.
source: Inhibition of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons also did not affect feeding (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) and appetitive behaviors (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: Silencing chloroquine-TRAPed (hM4Di+ve) CeA neurons with CNO injection in the chloroquine-paired chamber during conditioning blocked CPA to chloroquine, while CNO-treated mCherry controls exhibited CPA to chloroquine.
source: Silencing chloroquine-TRAPed (hM4Di+ve) CeA neurons with CNO injection in the chloroquine-paired chamber during conditioning blocked CPA to chloroquine, while CNO-treated mCherry controls exhibited CPA to chloroquine, suggesting that these neurons can robustly modulate the aversive component of itch (Figure 4h–k).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4h-k.

claim: Chloroquine-TRAPed CeA neurons can robustly modulate the aversive component of itch.
source: Silencing chloroquine-TRAPed (hM4Di+ve) CeA neurons with CNO injection in the chloroquine-paired chamber during conditioning blocked CPA to chloroquine, while CNO-treated mCherry controls exhibited CPA to chloroquine, suggesting that these neurons can robustly modulate the aversive component of itch (Figure 4h–k).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observation that silencing these neurons blocked CPA.

claim: Chloroquine-TRAPed CeA neurons send notably dense axonal projections in the ventral periaqueductal gray (vPAG).
source: We found that chloroquine-TRAPed CeA neurons send notably dense axonal projections in the ventral periaqueductal gray (vPAG) (Figure 5a–d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5a-d.

claim: Chloroquine-TRAPed CeA neurons send projections to the bed nucleus of stria terminalis (BNST), lateral hypothalamus and faint projection in substantia nigra and parabrachial nucleus (PBN).
source: We also observed projections to the bed nucleus of stria terminalis (BNST), lateral hypothalamus and faint projection in substantia nigra and parabrachial nucleus (PBN).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations described in the text.

claim: The vPAG has previously been shown to contribute to pruritic behaviors.
source: Because the vPAG has previously been shown to contribute to pruritic behaviors (Gao et al., 2019; Samineni et al., 2019), we focused our functional studies on this CeA→vPAG circuit.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Photostimulating ChR2-expressing chloroquine-TRAPed CeA neuronal terminals in the vPAG recapitulated spontaneous scratching behaviors.
source: As predicted, photostimulating ChR2-expressing chloroquine-TRAPed CeA neuronal terminals in the vPAG recapitulated spontaneous scratching behaviors (Figure 5e).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5e.

claim: Activating chloroquine-TRAPed CeA neuronal terminals in the vPAG did not produce freezing or flight responses.
source: Activating chloroquine-TRAPed CeA neuronal terminals in the vPAG did not produce freezing or flight responses.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations described in the text.

claim: Chloroquine-evoked scratching was potentiated with optical reactivation of CeA→vPAG projections while no changes were observed in the eYFP controls.
source: Chloroquine-evoked scratching was potentiated with optical reactivation of CeA→vPAG projections while no changes were observed in the eYFP controls (Figure 5f).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: The CeA→vPAG neuronal circuit is crucial node in mediating pruritic behaviors.
source: These results show that the CeA→vPAG neuronal circuit is crucial node in mediating pruritic behaviors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observations that stimulating this projection recapitulated and potentiated scratching behaviors.

claim: RNA-seq of chloroquine-activated CeA cells revealed significant enrichment of several unique transcripts in the chloroquine-activated neurons.
source: Subsequent analysis of chloroquine-TRAPed neurons revealed significant enrichment of several unique transcripts in the chloroquine-activated neurons (Figure 6b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Weighted gene correlation network analysis (WGCNA) of genes identified a cluster of upregulated genes 99% correlated and highly significant for chloroquine-activated neurons.
source: Weighted gene correlation network analysis (WGCNA) of genes identified a cluster of upregulated genes 99% correlated and highly significant for chloroquine-activated neurons (Figure 6—figure supplement 2f–h).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2f–h.

claim: KEGG and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) identified changes in the expression of functionally related candidate genes that are enriched in several pathways.
source: From KEGG and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), we have identified changes in the expression of functionally related candidate genes that are enriched in several pathways (Figure 6c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Considerable overlap was observed between Ntsr2+ve (75.31% cells per four sections), Gpr88+ve (69.35% cells per four sections) and Gabrg1+ve (62.32% cells per four sections) cells with chloroquine activated Fos+ve cells in the CeA.
source: We observed considerable overlap between Ntsr2+ve (75.31% cells per four sections), Gpr88+ve (69.35% cells per four sections) and Gabrg1+ve (62.32% cells per four sections) cells with chloroquine activated Fos+ve cells in the CeA (Figure 6d), which were shown to be significantly enriched in chloroquine-TRAPed tdTomato+ve cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: Partial overlap of Fos+ve cells in the CeA was found with cells that express Oprm1+ve (26.47% cells per four sections) Penk+ve (30.77% cells per four sections) and Chrm1+ve (36.50% cells per four sections).
source: We find their partial overlap of Fos+ve cells in the CeA (Figure 6e) with cells that express Oprm1+ve (26.47% cells per four sections) Penk+ve (30.77% cells per four sections) and Chrm1+ve (36.50% cells per four sections).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: Chloroquine-activated neurons in the central amygdala (CeA) are necessary and sufficient for both itch sensation and associated aversion.
source: Here, we show the necessity and sufficiency of chloroquine-activated neurons in the central amygdala (CeA) for both itch sensation and associated aversion.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Chloroquine-activated CeA neurons play important roles in itch-related comorbidities, including anxiety-like behaviors.
source: Further, we show that chloroquine-activated CeA neurons play important roles in itch-related comorbidities, including anxiety-like behaviors, but not in some aversive and appetitive behaviors previously ascribed to CeA neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Chloroquine-activated CeA neurons do not play a role in some aversive and appetitive behaviors previously ascribed to CeA neurons.
source: Further, we show that chloroquine-activated CeA neurons play important roles in itch-related comorbidities, including anxiety-like behaviors, but not in some aversive and appetitive behaviors previously ascribed to CeA neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: RNA-sequencing of chloroquine-activated CeA neurons identified several differentially expressed genes as well as potential key signaling pathways in regulating pruritis.
source: RNA-sequencing of chloroquine-activated CeA neurons identified several differentially expressed genes as well as potential key signaling pathways in regulating pruritis.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Chloroquine-activated CeA neurons send projections to the ventral periaqueductal gray that are critical in modulation of itch.
source: Finally, viral tracing experiments demonstrate that these neurons send projections to the ventral periaqueductal gray that are critical in modulation of itch.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Itch accompanies unpleasant sensations that evoke strong urges to scratch and promote learned avoidance behavior.
source: One such threat detection system is itch, which accompanies unpleasant sensations that evoke strong urges to scratch and promote learned avoidance behavior (Bautista et al., 2014; Han and Dong, 2014; Ikoma et al., 2006; LaMotte et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The CeA is molecularly heterogeneous and mediates diverse behaviors generally related to negative affect.
source: CeA neurons are molecularly heterogeneous and mediate diverse behaviors generally related to negative affect (John et al., 2015; Kalin et al., 2004; LeDoux, 2003; Ressler and Mayberg, 2007; Roozendaal et al., 2009; Tye et al., 2011), so we reasoned global manipulation of CeA neuronal activity would not provide the specificity needed to test the specific roles of chloroquine-activated neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Global manipulation of CeA neuronal activity would not provide the specificity needed to test the specific roles of chloroquine-activated neurons.
source: CeA neurons are molecularly heterogeneous and mediate diverse behaviors generally related to negative affect (John et al., 2015; Kalin et al., 2004; LeDoux, 2003; Ressler and Mayberg, 2007; Roozendaal et al., 2009; Tye et al., 2011), so we reasoned global manipulation of CeA neuronal activity would not provide the specificity needed to test the specific roles of chloroquine-activated neurons.
evidence: The claim is a logical inference based on the molecular heterogeneity of CeA neurons.

claim: Both tdTomato+ve and tdTomato-ve cells expressed Slc32A1 transcript (VGAT, a marker for GABAergic neurons).
source: In our sequencing results, we observed that both the tdTomato+ve and tdTomato-ve cells expressed Slc32A1 transcript (VGAT, a marker for GABAergic neurons), consistent with the notion that the majority of CeA neurons are GABAergic.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from RNA-seq.

claim: The majority of CeA neurons are GABAergic, consistent with RNA-seq data showing Slc32A1 transcript expression.
source: In our sequencing results, we observed that both the tdTomato+ve and tdTomato-ve cells expressed Slc32A1 transcript (VGAT, a marker for GABAergic neurons), consistent with the notion that the majority of CeA neurons are GABAergic.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: Anatomical tracing data indicate that CeA neurons that project to the PAG are GABAergic inhibitory populations.
source: Our RNA-seq data show that CeA neurons are GABAergic, and anatomical tracing data indicate that CeA neurons that project to the PAG are GABAergic inhibitory populations (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Recent work shows that CeA GABAergic neurons that project to vlPAG can elicit freezing, escape, hunting, sleep and nociception.
source: Recent work shows that CeA GABAergic neurons that project to vlPAG can elicit freezing, escape (Haubensak et al., 2010; Tovote et al., 2016), hunting (Han et al., 2017), sleep (Snow et al., 2017) and nociception (Avegno et al., 2018; Li and Sheets, 2018; Yin et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Chloroquine-activated CeA→PAG projections drive pruritic behaviors without evoking freezing or escape behaviors, suggesting that these FosTRAPed CeA→PAG projections are distinctly tuned to elicit scratching.
source: In our work, we found that the chloroquine-activated CeA→PAG projections drive pruritic behaviors without evoking freezing or escape behaviors, suggesting that these FosTRAPed CeA→PAG projections are distinctly tuned to elicit scratching.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: Activating Tac1 neurons in the PAG can drive robust scratching behaviors.
source: Recent work from Gao et al., 2019, suggests that activating Tac1 neurons can drive robust scratching behaviors; this suggests that there could be parallel circuits downstream of the CeA that can evoke and inhibit itch-evoked scratching.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Gao et al., 2019).

claim: There could be parallel circuits downstream of the CeA that can evoke and inhibit itch-evoked scratching.
source: Recent work from Gao et al., 2019, suggests that activating Tac1 neurons can drive robust scratching behaviors; this suggests that there could be parallel circuits downstream of the CeA that can evoke and inhibit itch-evoked scratching.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation based on prior work.

claim: Recent work in the VTA shows that pruritogen-evoked scratching elevates the activity of dopamine neurons, and this elevated activity is required for the hedonic aspects of pruritogen-evoked scratching.
source: Recent work in the VTA shows that pruritogen-evoked scratching elevates the activity of dopamine neurons, and this elevated activity is required for the hedonic aspects of pruritogen-evoked scratching (Su et al., 2019; Yuan et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The VTA sends projections to the CeA.
source: The VTA is known to send projections to the CeA.
evidence: The claim is based on established anatomical knowledge.

claim: VTA projections to the CeA could encode aversive aspects observed in the CeA.
source: It is possible that these projections encode aversive aspects that we have seen in the CeA (Leshan et al., 2010; Zhou et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to prior work.

claim: There are studies showing that scratching on the site of pruritogen application can suppress neural activity in spinothalamic neurons.
source: There is now literature suggesting that scratching on the site of pruritogen application can suppress neural activity in spinothalamic neurons (Davidson et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Davidson et al., 2009).

claim: In spinothalamic neurons, activity elicited by pruritogens can be completely abolished by scratching.
source: In these neurons, activity elicited by pruritogens can be completely abolished by scratching, suggesting that relief of itch by scratching results from suppression of activity in the spinal cord.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Relief of itch by scratching results from suppression of activity in the spinal cord.
